sentences.text: COMMON ORDER
These two Criminal Miscellaneous Cases are connected and therefore, I am disposing of these cases by a common order.

The petitioner in Crl.M.C.No.4657/2021 is the 1 st accused and the petitioner in Crl.M.C.No.6456/2018 is the 2 nd accused in C.C.No.1741/2014 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Ottappalam which arises from Crime No.406/2014 of the Sreekrishnapuram Police Station.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Ottappalam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The above case is charge sheeted against the petitioners alleging offence punishable under Section 420 r/w 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. The allegation in the complaint is that the 1st accused was in possession of cheque no.982081 with the State Bank of India, Katampazhipuram branch signed by the defacto complainant.

The same was obtained by the 2nd accused and the 1st Crl.M.C.Nos.6456/2018 and 4657/2021 2024:KER:75576 accused filed a complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act against the defacto complainant.
Hence, it is alleged that the accused committed the offences.

According to the petitioners, even if the entire allegations are accepted, no offence is made against the petitioners.
3.
Heard Senior Counsel Adv.K.Ramkumar, instructed by his retaining counsel and also the counsel appearing for the defacto complainant.
I also heard the Public Prosecutor.
4. The Senior Counsel submitted that, even if the entire allegations are accepted, no offence is made out against the petitioners.
The senior counsel submitted that, in effect, the case of the prosecution is that, for filing a complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, a cheating case is registered.
The senior counsel go to the extent of saying that the attempt of the prosecution amounts to contempt of court.
The senior counsel also submitted that, a civil proceeding is also initiated against the defacto complainant for recovery of amount based on the cheque.

The counsel appearing for the defacto complainant submitted that the Crl.M.C.Nos.6456/2018 and 4657/2021 2024:KER:75576 criminal prosecution initiated against the defacto complainant ended in acquittal and that itself show that it is a frivolous prosecution initiated by the accused against the defacto complainant.
Therefore, the offence under Section 420 IPC is not made out.
5. This Court considered the contentions of the petitioners, defacto complainant and the Public Prosecutor.

The admitted case as stated in the final report is extracted hereunder:

.' Crl.M.C.Nos.6456/2018 and 4657/2021 2024:KER:75576 6. Admittedly, the 1st accused filed the complaint.
There is nothing to connect the 2nd accused with the alleged offence except the statement of the defacto complainant.
I am of the considered opinion that, no offence under Section 420 IPC is attracted against the 2nd accused who is the petitioner in Crl.M.C.No.6456/2018.
But, I do not want to make any observation about the allegation against the 1st accused.
But, the 1st accused can file a discharge petition before the trial court.
If such a discharge petition is filed, there can be a direction to consider the same in accordance with law.

But,
as far as the 2 nd accused is concerned, as I mentioned earlier, the continuation of the prosecution is not necessary.

Therefore, these Criminal Miscellaneous Cases are disposed of with the following directions:
I.

Crl.M.C.No.6456/2018 is allowed and all further proceedings against the petitioner in C.C.No.1741/2014 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court,
Ottapalam arising from Crime No.406/2014 of Sreekrishnapuram Police Station are quashed.
